record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Decentralized causal reasoning for safety-critical MARL
record.original_question: How can embedding a causal model inside a multi-agent reinforcement-learning framework enable decentralized reasoning for safety-critical applications, such as healthcare systems in which practitioners pool resources and optimize healthcare policies, or robotic applications?

evidence.quote: Embedding a causal model in the multi-agent framework opens opportunity for decentralised reasoning in safety critical applications such as healthcare and robotic applications.

For example, consider how healthcare practitioners can pool resources (Rieke et al., 2020) and optimise their healthcare policies aided by a safe and interactive MARL systems (Holzinger, 2016). Bridged with other beneﬁts of explicit causal methods already discussed, this presents a promising front for future research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) setting formalized as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP) given by a tuple (N, S, {A_i}, P, {O_i}, {R_i}, γ), where N is a set of agents, S is a global state space, A_i and O_i are the action and observation spaces of agent i, P(s' | s, a) is the joint transition kernel, R_i is agent i's reward function, and γ ∈ (0,1) is a discount factor. Augment this setting with a structural causal model (SCM) M = (U, V, F, P(U)) whose endogenous variables V include the states, actions, observations and rewards, exogenous variables U capture unobserved confounders, and the structural equations F = {f_v}_{v ∈ V} encode the underlying causal mechanisms; M also induces interventional distributions P(· | do(·)) and counterfactual distributions.

Design a framework in which each agent i has access only to its local observation-action history and to (parts of) the causal graph G associated with M, and learns a decentralized policy π_i(a_i | o_{≤t}^i) such that:

(1) Decentralized causal reasoning: every agent can answer interventional and counterfactual queries about its own decisions using only locally available information and shared structural knowledge of G, without requiring centralized access to the joint state or to other agents' policies at execution time.

(2) Safety guarantees: there exists a specified set of unsafe events U ⊂ S × A and the joint policy π = (π_1, …, π_N) satisfies Pr_π(visit U) ≤ δ for a prescribed tolerance δ > 0, with the bound derivable from the causal model under distribution shift (i.e., shift between training and deployment environments).

(3) Applicability: the framework must be demonstrated on at least one of the following classes of problems:
   (a) a federated healthcare scenario, modeled as a Dec-POMDP in which agents represent institutions that share parameters/causal structure but not raw patient data, and jointly optimize a treatment policy subject to per-patient safety constraints; or
   (b) a multi-robot manipulation or navigation task with physical safety constraints and partial observability.

Problem. Construct such a framework — specifying (i) the representation of the causal model and how causal knowledge is shared between agents, (ii) the learning algorithm and its convergence/sample-complexity guarantees, and (iii) provable safety and decentralization properties — and prove that it satisfies (1)–(3). Equivalently, characterize the minimal causal information that must be communicated among agents to guarantee decentralized execution with the safety bound in (2), and prove a matching lower bound.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a forward-looking research direction rather than a precisely stated conjecture, and no comprehensive framework satisfying decentralized causal reasoning together with formal safety guarantees in MARL appears in the literature as of 2026. Causal MARL is an active but still-emerging area (e.g., works on causal influence detection, counterfactual credit assignment, and causal world models), but a unified, provably safe, decentralized causal MARL framework demonstrated on federated healthcare or multi-robot safety-critical tasks remains an open research program.
